open_questions: Panama's intro: D...'s tab (18645), followed here, puts the middle tom in eighths under rack-tom accents; Ghost's two tabs (865271, 1318689) put the floor tom on every beat. The record's intro is under a car's engine and was not settled by a beat track.

Hot for Teacher's intro: the Simmons pad and the triggered rototoms and bass drums of its first bars (Drumeo, as Wikipedia gives it) are left out; which parts of the rest of the intro are triggered is not settled.
The kit on 1984: the tabs name a Ludwig Vistalite; no source read names the kit or the snare used at 5150, nor the cymbals on any record.
Not scored: You Really Got Me (a Kinks cover), Dance the Night Away, Mean Street, Atomic Punk and the Sammy Hagar years (5150 to Balance), all with human tabs.

identity.name: Alex Van Halen
home_scenes: Pasadena and the Los Angeles clubs, 1972-1977
identity.summary: Van Halen's drummer from Mammoth in 1972 to his brother Eddie's death in 2020. Born in Amsterdam to a jazz saxophonist, raised in Pasadena, trained with Eddie as a classical pianist, he took up the drums on Eddie's kit and played them better. A big Ludwig kit with two bass drums, a snare he called the brown sound, the hat washing open in eighths, and a feel he said pushed the beat: Runnin' with the Devil and I'm the One's shuffle on both bass drums (1978), Everybody Wants Some!!'s tom groove (1980), Unchained (1981), and Jump, Panama and the double-bass shuffle of Hot for Teacher (1984).

traditions.impact: Both brothers were trained as classical pianists as children; he studied music theory, scoring and arranging at Pasadena City College.
His father Jan van Halen was a jazz saxophonist and clarinettist; he names Buddy Rich as an early and lifelong influence, and Billy Cobham.

traditions.tradition: British blues and hard rock drumming
traditions.impact: Ginger Baker, Keith Moon, Mitch Mitchell and John Bonham; Budgie's Ray Phillips.

eras.label: Mammoth and the clubs
eras.context: Mammoth, renamed Van Halen in 1974: backyard parties and Hollywood clubs, a demo produced by Gene Simmons, a Ludwig kit grown to two bass drums.
defining_traits: covers and originals in the clubs

eras.label: The David Lee Roth records
eras.context: Six albums with Ted Templeman, five cut quickly at Sunset Sound, 1984 at 5150: hard rock with a shuffle under it.
defining_traits: the hat washing open in eighths

eras.label: Sammy Hagar and after
eras.context: 5150 (1986) to Balance (1995) with Hagar, III with Gary Cherone, A Different Kind of Truth (2012) with Roth again; electronic pads added to the kit in the 1980s.

genres.name: Rock
genres.notes: Jump: a pop single on a rock kit.

evidence.note: "I'm the first to admit that I push the beat. The idea of trying to create strict metronomic time is nonsense."

swing.notes: Straight eighths in most songs; I'm the One and Hot for Teacher are shuffles at a full triplet (the record's kick, and the tabs' triplet feel). Modern Drummer hears his hat sixteenths as "sometimes slightly swung".

dynamics.balance: Loud throughout: the hat open, the crash ridden, a big snare; the tabs write almost no ghost notes.

feel_profile.interaction: Locked to Eddie's riffs: the snare and the kick placed with the guitar's accents in Unchained's pre-chorus and Jump's, the band's hits played with him.

hand_techniques.name: The hat open in eighths
hand_techniques.description: Ain't Talkin' 'bout Love's riff and verses, Panama's choruses: the hat washing open on every eighth.

hand_techniques.name: The crash ridden in eighths
hand_techniques.description: Unchained's choruses and pre-chorus: the crash in eighths over the kick in eighths.

hand_techniques.name: Tom grooves
hand_techniques.description: Everybody Wants Some!! and the intro of Panama: the toms in place of the hat and snare, over four on the floor.

foot_techniques.name: The double-bass shuffle
foot_techniques.description: Both bass drums on every swung eighth: I'm the One at 226 and Hot for Teacher at 257.

foot_techniques.name: The kick in eighths
foot_techniques.description: Unchained's verses and choruses: the kick on every eighth under the hat or the crash.

foot_techniques.name: The hat foot under the tom fills
foot_techniques.description: Runnin' with the Devil: the left foot on the hat under the fills round the toms.

coordination.notes: Two bass drums from 1977: every swung eighth of I'm the One and Hot for Teacher. The odd bars scored are Unchained's pre-chorus, where the song itself changes meter.

searched: Modern Drummer (2012), Consequence (2008), Van Halen Gear Timeline, Wikipedia (him, the albums, the songs)
devices_search.note: No cross-rhythm, grouping, polymeter or metric modulation is named or written. Jump's pre-chorus groups the kick, snare and hat in dotted quarters for two bars with the band's riff, a figure of the song; Unchained's bars of 6/4 and 7/4 are the song's meter.

voice_language.hihat: Half-opened on 2 in Runnin' with the Devil, open in eighths in Ain't Talkin' 'bout Love, half open over four on the floor in Panama's verses, opened on every beat in the shuffles.
voice_language.snare: On 2 and 4; on 2, 3, 5 and 6 in Unchained's 7/4 bars; a dotted quarter apart in Jump's pre-chorus; the brown sound, his word for its tone.
voice_language.kick: Pushing the "and"s in the straight songs, on every swung eighth on two bass drums in the shuffles, four on the floor in Panama and Everybody Wants Some!!.
voice_language.toms: Fills down the toms over the hat foot; grooves on the toms in Everybody Wants Some!! and Panama's intro.
voice_language.cymbals: The crash ridden in eighths, the ride bell in quarters and eighths in the choruses and solos, a china now and then.

implements.notes: Sticks in every song scored here.

aesthetic: A Ludwig with two bass drums, a 24" and a 26", their front heads off and muffled with felt, foam and tape
"Throaty, conga-esque snare sounds" and "the unmistakable pop of his snare"; "brown sound" was his word for his snare's tone
sound_profile.cymbal_character: Zildjians in the early days; crashes ridden in eighths and a ride bell, a china now and then.

sample_hints.hard_rock: A big kit played hard in a room for the Sunset Sound records; tighter and closer for 1984 at 5150.

signature_traits.label: The double-bass shuffle
signature_traits.description: Both bass drums on every swung eighth under the hat opened on every beat: I'm the One (1978) at 226, Hot for Teacher (1984) at 257, "the hard-driving double bass shuffle from hell".

signature_traits.label: The hat washing open
signature_traits.description: The hat open in eighths under the riff (Ain't Talkin' 'bout Love), half open over four on the floor (Panama), half-opened on the backbeat (Runnin' with the Devil): the cymbal hiss Modern Drummer hears in his records.

signature_traits.label: The tom groove
signature_traits.description: Everybody Wants Some!!'s "jungle" drums: the toms over four on the floor with no snare, later the way into Panama on stage.

signature_traits.label: Parts that follow the riff
signature_traits.description: The snare and kick placed with Eddie's riff where it turns: Unchained's pre-chorus in bars of six and seven, Jump's pre-chorus in dotted quarters across the bar line.

patterns.name: Runnin' with the Devil, the intro
patterns.function: The hat half-opened on 2, the second crash on 4, the kick on 1 and the "and" and "a" of 2 and the "and" of 3.

patterns.name: Ain't Talkin' 'bout Love, the riff
patterns.function: The hat open in eighths, washing, the kick on 1, its "and", the "and" of 2, 3, its "and" and the "and" of 4.

patterns.name: I'm the One, the verse
patterns.function: A shuffle at 226 on both bass drums: the kick on every swung eighth, the hat opened on every beat, the snare on 2 and 4.

patterns.name: Everybody Wants Some!!, the tom groove
patterns.function: The kick and the floor tom on every beat, the floor tom on the "and" of 1, the rack tom on 2, its "and" and 4, the middle tom on the "and" of 3 and of 4: no snare.

patterns.name: Unchained, the pre-chorus
patterns.function: A bar of 7/4 (the tab's 4/4 and 3/4): the crash in eighths, the snare on 2, 3, 5 and 6, the kick off the beat around it.

patterns.name: Jump, the pre-chorus
patterns.function: The kick, the snare and the open hat each a dotted quarter apart, across the bar line, over the ride bell.

patterns.name: Panama, the verse
patterns.function: The hat half-open in eighths over four on the floor.

patterns.name: Hot for Teacher, the verse
patterns.function: The double-bass shuffle at 257: the kick on every swung eighth, the hat opened on every beat, the snare on 2 and 4.

equipment.label: Ludwig Pro Beat, silver sparkle, two bass drums (1970-1979)

drums.muffling: front head off; felt strips, foam and tape
front head off; felt strips, foam and tape

equipment.layout_notes: A 1970 Pro Beat with a Supraphonic snare, grown to a seven-piece double-bass kit; the 26" bass drum from 1975. Used on the first two albums at Sunset Sound, then retired. A fan history, not his own account.

affiliations.name: Van Halen
affiliations.notes: Formed as Mammoth with Eddie in 1972, Van Halen from 1974; the brothers the only two constant members; disbanded a month after Eddie's death in October 2020.

aspects: a drummer with his own sound

evidence.note: "Ginger Baker's drums sounded like Ginger Baker's drums." (Modern Drummer, 2012)

aspects: the drummer as a front man

evidence.note: Hot for Teacher's intro is "reminiscent of drummer Billy Cobham's tune 'Quadrant 4'" (Wikipedia, the song).
Budgie's drummer (Wikipedia: "Alex was influenced by Budgie drummer Ray Phillips").

philosophy.idea: Push the beat: strict metronomic time is not the aim; a loud, lively feel makes the music breathe.
The instrument is a second voice, the way a drummer communicates; a drummer's drums should sound like that drummer.

contribution.description: Brought jazz-influenced nimbleness, galloping swing and skip-stone tom work ("Hot for Teacher") to arena hard rock; widely regarded as one of the greatest drummers and named as an influence by Mike Portnoy, Taylor Hawkins and Travis Barker.

innovations: The double-bass shuffle as a hard rock groove (I'm the One, 1978; Hot for Teacher, 1984)

accolades.award: Knight of the Order of the Netherlands Lion

common_misconceptions: "Brown sound" is usually said of Eddie's guitar; Alex coined it, for the sound of his snare (Wikipedia).

beatbreaker.default_kit_sound: A big kit played hard in a room; tighter and closer for 1984
generation_rules: Hard rock: the hat half-opened on 2 or open in eighths, the kick pushing the "and"s.
Shuffles on both bass drums, every swung eighth.
Fills down the toms over the hat foot, into a crash on 3 or on 1.
Straight, loud, a little ahead of the beat.

lineage_display.lineage_blurb: Ginger Baker, Keith Moon and Bonham, with Buddy Rich and Cobham underneath: Van Halen's drummer, and a model for Portnoy, Hawkins and Travis Barker.
